Texas Pacific Land to Acquire EagleRock in $3 Billion All-Stock Transaction
November 23, 2026
Texas Pacific Land Corporation (NYSE: TPL) has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire EagleRock Land, LLC (NYSE: EROK) in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $3 billion , expanding its land ownership, water infrastructure and royalty operations across the Permian Basin.
The transaction will combine two land and water management businesses with complementary holdings in the Midland and Delaware basins. The combined company is expected to own approximately 1 million fee surface acres, along with an additional 105,000 acres covered by water-related dedication agreements.
Under the merger agreement, EagleRock shareholders will receive 0.0831 shares of a newly formed holding company for each EagleRock Class A share. Based on Texas Pacific Land’s five-day volume-weighted average share price as of November 20, 2026, the exchange ratio represents approximately $23.56 per EagleRock share.
Holders of units in EagleRock Land Operating, LLC will receive shares at the same exchange ratio, with their paired EagleRock Class B shares canceled.
Existing Texas Pacific Land shareholders are expected to own approximately 86% of the combined company, while former EagleRock shareholders and operating company unitholders will hold approximately 14% on a fully diluted basis.
The transaction will involve a holding company reorganization under which New Titan Holdings, Inc. will become the publicly traded parent of both businesses. The holding company is expected to adopt the Texas Pacific Land Corporation name upon closing. Each existing TPL share will convert into one share of the new holding company.
The combined business will retain Texas Pacific Land’s board of directors and executive management team, with headquarters in Dallas.
EagleRock owns or controls approximately 288,000 acres across the Permian Basin, including roughly 59,000 fee-owned acres primarily in Lea County, New Mexico. The acquisition will expand Texas Pacific Land’s presence in the Delaware Basin and increase its Midland Basin surface acreage by nearly 40%.
EagleRock’s Midland Basin assets include approximately 220,000 barrels per day of produced water handling capacity through gathering, disposal and recycling infrastructure, along with approximately 130,000 barrels per day of non-potable water supply capacity.
Following the acquisition, Texas Pacific Land expects its combined water infrastructure platform to have approximately 1.5 million barrels per day of aggregate non-potable water sourcing and produced water treatment capacity, representing a 49% increase.
Combined water storage capacity is projected to reach approximately 68 million barrels, an increase of 79%.
The expanded acreage also includes approximately 37,600 future undrilled well locations within five miles of the combined properties, providing potential demand for water services, surface access and related infrastructure.
Texas Pacific Land expects the transaction to be accretive to estimated 2027 free cash flow per share before synergies.
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the combined businesses generated pro forma adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 83% and free cash flow margins of approximately 60%.
Management has identified approximately $45 million in potential annual run-rate benefits, consisting of $20 million in corporate cost savings and $25 million in additional revenue opportunities. Those anticipated benefits are excluded from the reported pro forma financial figures.
“This combination supports our strategy to build the premier land, water and royalty platform in the Permian Basin by adding complementary assets that we believe will deliver increased intrinsic value per share,” said Tyler Glover , chief executive officer of Texas Pacific Land.
The acquisition will also expand Texas Pacific Land’s commercial relationship with Double Eagle through long-term water service arrangements supported by approximately 105,000 acres of aggregate dedications.
EagleRock CEO Greg Pipkin said the combination will bring additional capabilities to customers while allowing EagleRock shareholders to participate in the combined company’s future performance.
In connection with the transaction, Texas Pacific Land’s board approved an increase in its share repurchase authorization to $500 million. The company expects to maintain a net cash position following the acquisition and intends to increase shareholder distributions through repurchases and regular dividend growth.
Both companies’ boards unanimously approved the merger agreement. EagleRock’s board has recommended that its shareholders vote in favor of the transaction, while no vote of Texas Pacific Land shareholders is required.
EagleRock equity holders representing more than 50% of its outstanding voting power, including Double Eagle, have entered into voting and support agreements supporting the merger. Those shareholders are also subject to staggered lock-up arrangements extending through 12 months after closing.
The acquisition is expected to close during the first half of 2027, subject to EagleRock shareholder approval, expiration or termination of the applicable Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust waiting period and other customary closing conditions.
The transaction is intended to be tax-free to EagleRock shareholders and operating company unitholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
Evercore is serving as exclusive financial advisor to Texas Pacific Land, with Sidley Austin LLP and Haynes Boone, LLP providing legal counsel.
Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is serving as exclusive financial advisor to EagleRock, while Vinson & Elkins LLP is providing legal counsel.

Sierra's constellation-of-models architecture routes tasks across 15 or more models to optimize latency and quality.
Sierra announced on November 23, 2026 that it is raising $1.75 billion in Series F funding at a $30 billion valuation, in a round led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company builds AI agents that handle customer interactions and carry out business tasks for large enterprises.
The terms follow Sierra’s May 4, 2026 announcement that it was raising $950 million, led by Tiger Global and GV, at a valuation above $15 billion. Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV and Tiger Global are participating again after previously serving as lead investors.
Enterprise Growth Behind the Round
Sierra reported on October 30, 2026 that annual recurring revenue (ARR) had passed $400 million, including more than $150 million added in the third quarter. That quarterly addition exceeded the ARR it added during the entire prior year.
The company said ARR took six months to double from $100 million to $200 million, then five months to double from $200 million to $400 million.
Customer adoption has accompanied that growth. Sierra reported working with more than 40% of the Fortune 50 in May and almost 50% by the October update. The latter disclosure also described a large US retailer with more than $40 billion in revenue going from its first meeting with Sierra to a live agent in 27 days.
The May announcement supplied further deployment measures: Nordstrom launched its Nora voice agent in five weeks; Singtel launched in 10 weeks with resolution rates above 70%; and Cigna entered production in eight weeks while reducing patient-authentication time by 80%.
Outcome Pricing and Its Constraints
Sierra’s outcome-based pricing charges for results such as a resolved problem, originated loan, paid insurance claim or retained subscriber, rather than basing its core model on seats, tokens or usage. The company says this aligns its incentives with customers’ business results, while making attrition and margin more directly sensitive when promised results are not delivered.
Sierra also describes the approach as more complex operationally, contractually and for accounting than seat- or consumption-based pricing. It works only when software is highly autonomous and the outcome can be cleanly attributed to it; Sierra retains consumption-style pricing where that better fits the problem.
Ghostwriter and the Model Architecture
Ghostwriter sits above that pricing model. Sierra says teams define goals and guardrails, and the system builds, tests and deploys agents. A September 28, 2026 update made Ghostwriter proactive inside Slack and Teams: it can review customer conversations, recommend changes and experiments, monitor results and identify when those results are statistically significant.
Sierra says its constellation-of-models architecture assembles agents from 15 or more frontier, open-weight and proprietary models, selecting different models for tasks such as low-latency tool calling, classification, long-context reasoning and tone. Its Agent OS orchestrates those tasks, applies supervisors for guardrails and quality checks, and tracks provider latency, errors and timeouts so traffic can fail over to healthier models when a provider degrades.
The financing ultimately ties Sierra’s growth story to execution: rapid deployments supply the customer base, while its pricing model requires agents to operate autonomously and produce clearly attributable results.

India’s artificial intelligence (AI) funding has nearly doubled in 2026, but the sharp rise in investment has not necessarily translated into a wider pool of startups attracting capital. Instead, a handful of large funding rounds have accounted for most of the money flowing into the sector, even as the overall number of deals has declined.
Everything you need to know about this story Summary, key takeaways, timeline, glossary and FAQs — all in one place.

Indian AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding between January and September 2026, a 96% increase from the $822 million raised in the corresponding period last year, according to Tracxn’s latest report. The funding was also 162% higher than the $616 million raised in the first nine months of 2024, making it the highest total for any corresponding nine-month period since 2019.
The rise in funding has not translated into more deals for India's AI startups. In fact, the number of funding rounds fell 42% to 87 in the first nine months of 2026, from 149 a year ago. What changed was the size of the cheques. The average deal value climbed to $18.5 million from $5.5 million, indicating that investors are putting substantially more money into a smaller pool of companies.

A closer look at the deals shows just how concentrated the funding has been. The 10 largest rounds together brought in $1.5 billion, accounting for 90% of the total raised by Indian AI companies. Neysa, a Mumbai-based AI cloud provider, led the pack with its $600 million Series B in February. The round alone made up 37% of all AI funding during the period and contributed 76% of the increase in funding over the year-ago period. Sarvam, the Bengaluru-based generative AI startup, was another major recipient, raising $255 million in a Series B in June and a further $90.4 million in August. Yotta also secured $150 million in a Series D round in July.
The flip side of these large transactions is that fewer companies are getting funded. The number of startups receiving funding for the first time dropped 60% to 24, compared with 60 in the first nine months of 2025. Series A and later-stage deals also became fewer, falling 33% to 24 from 36.

Tanglin backs Matters.AI
Matters.AI, which is building an AI security engineer for data, has raised about Rs 115 crore ($12 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, per an announcement.
IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures and Tetration Ventures also participated, alongside existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners.
The latest round takes the company’s total funding to about Rs 175 crore ($18.25 million).
AI agents now read, copy and move enterprise data with the permissions of the employees who run them. Most data security tools show where sensitive data sits. They do not show who or what is using it, or why, so security teams connect alerts from separate tools by hand before they can respond.
“Security teams don’t need another tool telling them something might be wrong. They need a system that understands the problem, investigates it, and takes action,” said Keshava Murthy, Co-Founder and CEO of Matters.AI, in a statement.
Ionic Wealth raises funding from parent
Ionic Wealth, the wealth management platform backed by Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in strategic funding from its parent company and a group of family offices.
The fundraise takes the platform’s total funding to Rs 466 crore, Angel One said in a media statement.
Ionic Wealth claims to have crossed Rs 16,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with a combined high-net-worth individual (HNI) and ultra-high-net-worth individual (UHNI) client base of more than 2,900 across over 12 cities. The platform has a team of more than 100 private bankers and has achieved this scale within two years of operations.
The company plans to use the funding to strengthen its portfolio-led offerings and global capabilities, integrate AI into its wealth-tech platform, scale its UHNI business and expand its presence in India and overseas.
“This strategic investment validates our vision of building a new-age wealth platform at the intersection of domain expertise and technology,” said Srikanth Subramanian, Co-founder and CEO of Ionic Wealth, in a media statement.

Draper Receives $315.7 Million For Trident II Guidance Engineering

candidates.text:
Crowley Government Services Wins $270.4 Million Navy Vessel Operations Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:54 PM
Crowley Government Services Wins $270.4 Million Navy Vessel Operations Contract
Crowley Government Services has received a $270.4 million contract from the U.S. Navy’s Military Sealift Command to operate and maintain six government-owned vessels supporting ocean surveillance and missile-range instrumentation missions. The firm-fixed-price contract includes pass-through elements and covers services performed at locations worldwide.
The award supports the continued operation of specialized vessels that provide important capabilities for U.S. naval surveillance, testing, and national defense activities.
Crowley Government Services will be responsible for operating and maintaining the vessels under the contract’s requirements, supporting their availability for assigned missions.
The contract includes an initial six-month performance period beginning December 1, 2026, with provisions allowing services to continue through May 2028 if the available extensions are exercised.
Six-Vessel Fleet
The contract covers five ocean-surveillance vessels and one missile-range instrumentation ship.
The ocean-surveillance vessels include USNS Victorious, USNS Able, USNS Effective, USNS Loyal, and USNS Impeccable.
The sixth vessel is USNS Howard O. Lorenzen, a missile-range instrumentation ship supporting specialized defense-related monitoring and measurement missions.
Ocean-surveillance vessels provide capabilities that support the Navy’s understanding of maritime activity and underwater operating environments.
These ships contribute to the broader surveillance infrastructure used to support naval operations and situational awareness.
Missile-range instrumentation vessels serve a different but complementary mission, providing specialized platforms for collecting data associated with missile testing and related defense activities.
Operating these vessels requires sustained maintenance, qualified maritime personnel, and coordination with Military Sealift Command to support operational requirements.
Through the contract, Crowley Government Services will provide operational and maintenance services intended to help keep the six vessels available for their assigned missions.
Contract Period And Extension Options
The initial firm period runs from December 1, 2026, through May 31, 2027.
The contract includes one six-month option that, if exercised, would extend performance through November 30, 2027.
A separate six-month extension available under federal acquisition regulations could further continue services through May 30, 2028.
These provisions give the Navy flexibility to maintain operational continuity while determining its longer-term requirements for the vessels.
The announced $270.4 million contract value reflects the overall award structure, including the described extension provisions.
However, compensation associated with optional performance periods depends on whether the government exercises those options.
The agreement will use fiscal 2027 Navy working-capital funding. The contract announcement did not specify the amount initially obligated at the time of award.
Sole-Source Procurement
Military Sealift Command awarded the contract without competition under a federal procurement exception allowing a sole-source award when only one responsible source can satisfy the government’s requirements.
The procurement approach reflects the Navy’s determination that the applicable statutory conditions for a noncompetitive award were met.
The contract establishes Crowley Government Services as the provider responsible for the specified vessel operations and maintenance services during the applicable performance periods.
Military Sealift Command, headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity.
The award is identified under contract number N3220527C1202.
The agreement represents a substantial government maritime services contract supporting specialized naval capabilities.
By covering five ocean-surveillance ships and a missile-range instrumentation vessel, the award supports the operation of platforms used for surveillance, technical monitoring, and defense-related missions.
The contract also underscores the Navy’s continued reliance on commercial maritime service providers to operate and maintain government-owned vessels.

Prince George’s County Approves $215M Financing Plan for $1.4B Sphere at National Harbor
November 23, 2026
The proposed 6,000-seat entertainment venue advances as county officials seek new tax revenue, tourism growth and economic development.
The Sphere in Las Vegas
Prince George’s County has taken a major step toward bringing a $1.4 billion Sphere entertainment venue to National Harbor , with the County Council unanimously approving a $215 million financing package to support the development.
The proposed 6,000-seat venue, modeled after the high-tech Sphere in Las Vegas, would become a major new entertainment destination along the Potomac River, approximately 44 miles south of downtown Baltimore.
The financing approval follows months of negotiations over public investment, labor protections, local hiring and community benefits.
$215 Million Financing Package
Under the approved plan, Prince George’s County would issue $215 million in bonds backed by anticipated increases in tax revenues from the National Harbor area.
About $130 million of the proceeds would support construction of the Sphere, while the remaining financing would refinance existing debt.
The county would repay the tax increment financing bonds through designated revenues, including property taxes generated by increases in assessed property values.
Sphere Entertainment Co. has argued that public financing is necessary to make National Harbor competitive with other potential venue locations.
Economic Development and Tax Revenue
County Executive Aisha Braveboy has positioned the Sphere as an opportunity to diversify the county’s economy and offset anticipated revenue losses associated with the Washington Commanders’ planned departure and the closure of Six Flags.
Braveboy said the project could generate more than three times the tax revenue the county expects to lose from those developments.
Beyond ticket sales, the venue could stimulate additional spending at National Harbor hotels, restaurants, retail establishments and other businesses.
The development would also expand the region’s entertainment infrastructure, potentially attracting concerts, immersive productions, corporate events and visitors from across the Mid-Atlantic.
Local Business Participation and Employment
The financing agreement includes provisions designed to increase participation by Prince George’s County businesses and residents.
The project establishes several construction-related targets:
50% of eligible construction spending directed to county-based small businesses or locally owned and operated businesses.
40% of eligible construction spending targeted toward county-based minority businesses on a best-effort basis.
45% of eligible construction work hours targeted toward Prince George’s County residents on a best-effort basis.
Council members also agreed to communicate additional local business participation goals to the county executive.
Labor organizations welcomed provisions protecting hospitality and service workers’ ability to organize but expressed concerns about the absence of a formal Project Labor Agreement covering construction employment.
UNITE HERE Local 25, which represents hotel, restaurant and casino workers, supported labor peace provisions while criticizing the lack of stronger construction worker protections.
Community Impact Fund Established
The County Council also approved a community impact fund intended to address infrastructure, transportation and neighborhood concerns associated with the project.
The fund would receive 15% of qualifying county revenues generated by the Sphere, including certain admissions and amusement taxes and property tax revenues not already committed to bond repayment.
Funding would be divided equally between two categories:
50% for community programs and services
50% for infrastructure and capital improvements
Communities located within six miles of the venue would be eligible.
The council resolution did not establish a specific dollar amount for the fund.
Public Financing Draws Scrutiny
Despite unanimous council approval, the proposal has faced opposition from residents concerned about the county’s financial exposure and competing infrastructure priorities.
Critics questioned whether projected economic benefits would justify the public investment, particularly given National Harbor’s existing commercial success.
Other residents argued that the county should prioritize infrastructure improvements in communities outside the waterfront development district.
Supporters, including Councilmember Jolene Ivey, maintain that the Sphere could help reduce the county’s reliance on residential property taxes by expanding commercial activity and diversifying revenue sources.
A Major Addition to National Harbor
If completed, the National Harbor Sphere would represent one of Maryland’s most significant entertainment investments.
The proposed venue would build on the international visibility of the Las Vegas Sphere, which combines immersive digital displays, advanced audio technology and large-scale live entertainment.
For Prince George’s County, the project represents a broader economic development strategy centered on tourism, hospitality, commercial investment and a more diversified tax base.
The council’s financing approval marks an important milestone, although construction timing and other development details remain to be finalized.
Key Takeaways
$1.4 billion: Estimated total project investment.
$215 million: County-approved bond financing package.
$130 million: Portion of financing designated to support Sphere construction.
6,000 seats: Planned capacity of the National Harbor venue.
50%: Minimum target for eligible construction spending with county-based small or locally owned businesses.
15%: Share of qualifying county revenues designated for the community impact fund.

AIVC Launches With $112 Million in Strategic Investment to Build AI-Focused Companies
November 23, 2026
AIVC (AI Value Creation) has emerged from stealth with $112 million in strategic investment , backed by a family office and members of its leadership team, to support artificial intelligence-driven business transformation and the development of new companies.
The investment will fund AIVC’s operations across three interconnected activities: transforming existing businesses through AI, developing reusable technology based on those engagements and launching independent companies through its venture studio.
A majority of the capital will be allocated to AIVC’s Studio, which plans to establish three to five companies annually. The firm intends to identify commercial opportunities through its work with existing businesses before committing resources to new ventures.
AIVC was founded by RC Willenbrock, its chief executive officer and a former partner and head of AIxPE at Boston Consulting Group. David Sukhin, previously head of AI at Citadel, leads the firm’s venture studio.
The company has assembled a team of operators, engineers and research scientists with experience at Citadel, Millennium, Palantir, BCG, Nike, Lemonade, Airbnb and American Express.
Unlike traditional consulting firms that primarily provide advisory services, AIVC combines operational execution with technology development and company ownership. Its model is designed to link compensation and investment returns to measurable business outcomes rather than the volume of AI technology deployed.
“AI is a compression engine: it shrinks the time and effort that routine work consumes,” said Willenbrock. “But whether that reaches the bottom line depends on what a company does with the capacity it frees. We do not want AI to replace what makes people valuable. We want it to make people more human.”
The firm’s approach emphasizes using AI to automate routine processes while redirecting employee capacity toward higher-value activities, customer service and business growth.
Within its venture studio, AIVC plans to develop companies around commercial problems identified and tested through its operating engagements. The strategy is intended to establish customer demand and technical feasibility before launching new businesses.
“The two hardest parts of building new companies are (1) knowing which problems deserve to become a company and (2) identifying the most exceptional people to solve them,” said Sukhin.
AIVC said its current engagements are on pace to generate more than $1 billion in enterprise value, primarily through business growth and increased operating capacity rather than workforce reductions. That figure represents the firm’s projected value creation, not realized investment returns or independently verified financial results.
The company said it will prioritize engagements where potential financial benefits can be measured and where clients are prepared to implement and sustain operational changes.
AIVC did not disclose the identity of its family office investor, the ownership stakes associated with the $112 million investment or the valuation assigned to the company.

candidates.text:
Compuvi Reaches $50 Million Valuation Following Consulta Ventures Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:55 AM
Compuvi Reaches $50 Million Valuation Following Consulta Ventures Investment
Compuvi has reached a $50 million post-money valuation after securing an investment from Consulta Ventures through a pre-Series A bridge round.
The San Francisco-based enterprise AI company plans to use the investment and Consulta’s strategic support to strengthen its global commercial operations, sales organization, and customer success infrastructure. Compuvi will also continue developing its technology as it prepares for a Series A financing.
Expanding Preventive Compliance Technology
Compuvi develops Confinaid, an AI-powered platform designed to identify potential legal and regulatory risks within corporate communications, documents, and workflows before violations occur.
The platform analyzes the context of emails, enterprise messages, and documents to identify risks involving areas such as competition law, data protection, employment law, and financial regulation. Confinaid can alert employees in real time, route potentially problematic content to legal or compliance teams, and prevent certain communications from being sent.
Unlike conventional compliance tools that rely heavily on keywords or detect violations after they happen, Confinaid applies contextual analysis to support a preventive approach.
Consulta’s involvement will extend beyond financial backing. Its partners will work with Compuvi to develop scalable sales processes and customer success capabilities while helping the company expand its enterprise customer base in the United States and Europe.
Compuvi has approximately 20 employees across the United States, Europe, and Türkiye. Its customers operate in regulated industries including financial services, healthcare, retail, telecommunications, energy, and legal services.
KEY QUOTES:
“What Consulta and Compuvi have in common is that we understand the importance of the problem we are addressing not only in theory, but through its real impact on business processes. Compliance is becoming an increasingly critical management priority for organizations. We are developing a new approach that makes it possible to address risks before they emerge, rather than managing them after the fact.”
“Consulta’s firsthand experience of this need and its confidence in our solution make this collaboration particularly meaningful to us. By working together, we will build stronger and more scalable sales, marketing and customer success operations. We believe this investment will make an important contribution to our long-term strategic roadmap. In the coming period, our focus will be on accelerating our growth in global markets as we prepare for our Series A.”
Ataberk Ciftlikli, Founder and CEO of Compuvi

Vigor Marine Wins Contract Worth Up To $45.4 Million For USNS Lucy Stone Work
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:57 AM
Vigor Marine Wins Contract Worth Up To $45.4 Million For USNS Lucy Stone Work
Military Sealift Command has awarded Vigor Marine a $39.1 million firm-fixed-price contract for post-shakedown work on the fleet replenishment oiler USNS Lucy Stone.
The base contract covers a 137-calendar-day shipyard availability following the vessel’s initial operational period. Five unexercised options could increase the contract’s total cumulative value to approximately $45.4 million.
Post-Shakedown Availability
Post-shakedown availabilities are conducted after newly delivered vessels have completed initial operations and testing. The work commonly addresses deficiencies discovered during that period and completes repairs, modifications, inspections, and adjustments needed to prepare a ship for sustained service.
The award announcement did not provide a detailed list of the individual tasks Vigor will perform on USNS Lucy Stone.
Work will be conducted at Vigor’s facilities in Portland, Oregon, beginning January 18, 2027. The availability is scheduled to conclude on June 3, 2027.
The Navy obligated the full $39.1 million base-contract value at the time of the award using fiscal 2027 operations-and-maintenance funding. Those funds are scheduled to expire at the end of the current fiscal year.
The approximately $6.3 million associated with the five options has not been obligated. That additional value would only become funded contract work if Military Sealift Command exercises the applicable options.
The firm-fixed-price structure establishes an agreed amount for the base scope, placing responsibility on Vigor to perform the specified work within that price, subject to any government-authorized changes.
The government competed the procurement through its contracting portal and received two proposals.
Military Sealift Command in Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity. The contract number is N3220527C0005.

candidates.text:
Korte Construction Wins $38 Million Fort Gordon Barracks Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:39 AM
Korte Construction Wins $38 Million Fort Gordon Barracks Contract
The U.S. Army has awarded Korte Construction a $38 million contract to replace existing facilities with two new barracks at Fort Gordon, Georgia.
The fixed-price-award-fee contract uses a design-build-to-budget delivery approach. Its scope includes demolishing existing infrastructure and designing and constructing the two replacement barracks.
Military Housing Modernization
All work will be performed at Fort Gordon, with completion expected by September 26, 2029.
The Army obligated the contract’s entire $38 million value at the time of the award using fiscal 2027 military-construction funding. This means the announced value represents funded work rather than an unfunded maximum ceiling.
The procurement attracted 13 bids, indicating substantial competition for the construction project. Korte’s award was one of the more heavily competed projects included in the supplied group of military contracts.
The project will replace aging facilities with two modern barracks intended to support the Army’s service-member housing requirements at Fort Gordon. The award announcement did not disclose the planned square footage, resident capacity, configuration, or amenities of the new buildings.
Under the design-build-to-budget approach, the project’s design and construction will be coordinated within the Army’s established funding limit. This model is intended to align the final design with available resources while allowing construction considerations to be incorporated earlier in project development.
The fixed-price-award-fee structure establishes a defined contract price while allowing Korte to earn additional fees based on performance criteria established by the government. These criteria can include areas such as quality, cost control, schedule management, and overall contract execution.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ Savannah District is the contracting activity. The contract number is W912HN-27-C-A004.

British Columbia and Pelly Crossing, Yukon--(Newsfile Corp. - November 23, 2026) - Selkirk Copper Mines Inc. SCMI (FSE: IO20) (OTCQX: SKRKF) ("Selkirk Copper" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has entered into a binding term sheet (the "Term Sheet") with Queen's Road Capital Investment Ltd. ("Queen's Road") for a private placement (the "Offering") of US$30 million (approximately CAD$42.9 million) principal amount of unsecured convertible debentures (the "Debentures") of the Company.
Proceeds from the Offering will be used to fund the exploration, development, and restart of the Company's Minto Project located in central Yukon and for general corporate purposes.
M. Colin Joudrie, President & CEO of the Company, commented: "Queen's Road is a seasoned investor and financing partner to the mining industry with a track record of recognizing and investing in high-quality exploration and development companies through the cycle. The investment by Queen's Road is another step in our planned approach to the restart of mining and mineral processing activities that will deliver high-quality copper-gold-silver concentrates in a timely manner into a global market that is short of concentrate. Further, the investment by Queen's Road is a vote of confidence in our plan and recognition of the good work completed by our team over the last 18 months."
Warren Gilman, Chairman and CEO of Queen's Road, commented: "Queen's Road is delighted to work with Selkirk Copper and the Selkirk First Nation to see the restart of the Minto Mine become a reality. Minto represents a classic Queen's Road investment, a tested copper producer in a supportive jurisdiction with experienced and aligned partners. I have known and worked with Colin Joudrie for many years and look forward to supporting his Selkirk Copper team."
The Debentures will be governed by a debenture certificate to be issued by the Company in favor of Queen's Road and which will set out the terms contained in the Term Sheet. The Debentures will be convertible at the option of the holder, in part or in whole, into common shares of the Company at a price per share of CAD$1.00, based on the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate and subject to adjustment under certain events (the "Conversion Price"). The Conversion Price represents a 37% premium to the daily volume-weighted average trading price ("VWAP") of the Company's shares on the TSXV on November 20, 2026, being the last trading day before execution of the Term Sheet. The Company will be entitled to redeem the Debentures at par within a period of fourteen days following the third anniversary of the date of the issuance of the Debentures. Should the Company exercise its right to redeem the Debentures during this period, the holders are entitled to convert all of the outstanding Debentures into Common Shares at a price per share of C$0.92, equal to a 20% premium to the 3-day volume-weighted average trading price ("VWAP") at the date of this announcement.
The Debentures will bear interest (the "Interest") at a rate of 11% per annum, payable quarterly, over a 5-year term. 8.5% interest will be payable in cash and 2.5% interest will be payable in common shares of the Company, at the greater of the VWAP of the common shares of the Company on the TSX Venture Exchange (or other such Canadian stock exchange on which the Company's shares may be listed from time to time) (the "TSXV") for the 20 trading days ending on the last trading day prior to the date on which such interest is due, and the minimum price permitted by the policies of the TSXV.
Queen's Road QRC is a dividend paying, leading financier to the global resource sector. The Company is a resource-focused investment company, making investments in privately held and publicly traded resource companies. Queen's Road acquires and holds securities for long-term capital appreciation, with a focus on convertible debt securities and resource projects in advanced development or production located in safe jurisdictions. Queen's Road is a critical supporter of several base metal and precious metal projects including Adriatic Metals Plc, Los Andes Copper Ltd. and Moxico Copper Resources Plc.
In connection with the Offering and, subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals (including the TSXV), the Company will enter into an investor rights agreement with Queen's Road containing provisions relating to, among other things, voting alignment, standstill and transfer restriction covenants. At closing of the Offering, the Company will also pay to Queen's Road in cash or common shares, at the option of Queen's Road, an establishment fee of 3% of the principal amount of the Debentures.
Closing of the Offering is subject to customary closing conditions, including the completion of business, legal and financial due diligence satisfactory to Queen's Road, the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals (including the TSXV), the completion of definitive documentation (which shall include other customary terms for a transaction of this nature), and there being no material adverse change in the business of the Company, or a major event of national or international consequence that disrupts the financial markets or the business, operations or affairs of the Company

Selkirk First Nation is centered in Pelly Crossing, a community in central Yukon, 280 km north of Whitehorse. Why it matters
The funds support local cancer research, including projects selected through a competitive grant process that benefits the Cleveland community. Sustained philanthropic support helps the region's health system pursue research that might otherwise lack funding.
VeloSano's 2026 total of $20.2 million came from more than 30,000 donors making direct or legacy gifts, with more than 5,000 participants and volunteers supporting its signature events. The source does not specify the breakdown between event proceeds and direct donations.

Cleveland Clinic

The details
VeloSano funds are partly awarded through a competitive application process called VeloSano Pilot Grants. Residents who want to participate can register for 2027 VeloSano events beginning March 9. Donations and event participation directly support cancer research at Cleveland Clinic and Cleveland Clinic Children's.

Cancer research funding in Cleveland depends heavily on recurring community giving, and participation in events like Bike to Cure is one concrete way residents can contribute. Supporting local fundraisers helps sustain research pipelines beyond any single year's total.

Huntington Ingalls Receives $20 Million Across Submarine And Cruiser Support Awards
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 9:06 PM
Huntington Ingalls Receives $20 Million Across Submarine And Cruiser Support Awards
Huntington Ingalls received two Navy modifications totaling approximately $20 million for submarine-valve engineering and cruiser planning-yard support.
The company’s Newport News business received a $10.1 million modification for engineering and design work involving standard Navy valves installed on nuclear-powered submarines.
Two Naval Engineering Programs
Work on the submarine-valve effort will be performed in Newport News, Virginia. The Navy obligated $1.5 million in fiscal 2027 operations-and-maintenance funding at award, with that initial amount scheduled to expire at the end of the fiscal year.
Huntington Ingalls’ Ingalls Shipbuilding division received a separate $9.8 million modification exercising the seventh option year for CG-47-class integrated planning-yard services.
The work includes design, planning, and material support for cruiser maintenance and modernization. It will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, through December 2027.
No funding was obligated when the option was exercised. The Navy expects to commit funds as specific requirements arise.
The option was awarded without competition because the government determined that only one responsible source could provide the required services.
Naval Sea Systems Command in Washington is the contracting activity for both awards.
The combined $20 million reflects the announced modification values, while only $1.5 million was expressly obligated at the time of the two announcements.

candidates.snippet: Ramaphosa’s R100-million technology plan raises hopes for jobs Scrolla.Africa
candidates.text:
News
Ramaphosa’s R100-million technology plan raises hopes for jobs
President Cyril Ramaphosa during his visit to Silicon Valley in the United States, where he announced plans for a R100-million technology fund. Picture: The Presidency
By
Palesa Matlala
23rd November 2026
Share
5 Min Read
LANGUAGE:
English

Translating…
Listen to this article.
President Cyril Ramaphosa says entrepreneurs have proposed a R100-million fund to help South African businesses develop artificial intelligence and compete internationally.
With 8.6 million South Africans unemployed, experts say better training and work experience are needed to help young people find jobs.
Millions of South Africans are desperate for jobs, and President Cyril Ramaphosa believes new technology could help create opportunities for young people.
The president has announced plans for a R100-million fund to support South African businesses developing artificial intelligence.
The announcement follows his week-long visit to Silicon Valley in the United States, where he met technology companies and investors.
Artificial intelligence is technology that helps computers perform tasks such as answering questions, solving problems and working with information.
Ramaphosa said South African entrepreneurs who joined the trip proposed the fund.
“We walk away from Silicon Valley with commitments made by some of our own entrepreneurs that have come up with an idea that we should set up a venture capital fund that will start off with R100 million,” he said.
The money would help small technology businesses develop products, grow and possibly employ more people.
But South Africa faces a much bigger challenge.
According to Statistics South Africa, 8.6 million people were unemployed between July and September 2026. The unemployment rate stood at 33.7%.
For many young people, finding work remains difficult even after completing their studies.
A World Bank report published in August 2026 found that South Africa has unemployed graduates while some technology companies struggle to find workers with the right skills.
The report identified shortages in computer programming, networking and online security skills.
It also found that employers want people who can communicate well, solve problems and work with others.
The findings point to a possible solution: train unemployed young people in skills that businesses actually need.
Schools, colleges and universities could work more closely with employers to offer practical training and work experience.
Technology companies receiving government support could also be encouraged to hire and train young South Africans.
Another option is to make technology training available in townships and rural communities, where young people may struggle to afford computers, data and transport.
Community centres, libraries and schools could offer affordable Internet access and basic computer lessons.
Small businesses also need support.
Young people running businesses in townships could benefit from easier access to funding, business training and opportunities to sell their products and services.
But technology alone will not solve unemployment.
Economists at Nedbank, in their November 2026 labour market report, warned that businesses were not creating enough jobs to keep up with the growing number of people looking for work.
The report showed that South Africa gained 101,000 jobs in the third quarter, but the number of unemployed people still increased.
Ramaphosa believes the country has the talent to compete internationally.
“South Africa has talented startup founders who have come with us on this journey and who are developing innovative products with the potential to scale globally,” he said.
During his visit, the president met representatives from Google, Microsoft and Cisco.
He also held discussions about attracting more investment into South Africa’s technology industry.
The government wants to use artificial intelligence to improve healthcare, education and public services.
But the trip has faced criticism because Ramaphosa did not meet some of the world’s biggest technology bosses, including OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman.
Despite this, the president believes the visit was successful.
“We have used this visit to position South Africa as a major player in the AI economy, not merely a bystander,” he said.
The proposed R100-million fund has not yet been launched, and no date has been announced for businesses to apply.
The government has also not said how many jobs the fund could create.
For millions of unemployed South Africans, the biggest test will not be how much money is promised, but whether the investment leads to real jobs and opportunities.
